title: Who uses it, and where
caption: Who uses a skill, and where, decides what goes inside it and how much care it needs.
analogy: One card moves from your notebook to the fleet manual; project cards stay in the project binder.

Personal and general: a card box beside the pinned dive plan. Shared and project-specific: a project binder in front of the ship. Shared and general: the fleet manual with three ships; a dashed path carries the card from the notebook into the manual, where it gains an owner tag.

where-a-skill-is-stored.header: Storage scope can shape who gets a skill
where-a-skill-is-stored.description: In Claude Code, skills in the home directory are available across projects, repository skills are shared with collaborators, and plugins or managed settings can distribute skills to a team [1]. Codex documents repository and user skill locations too [2]. These are product examples; availability and team governance vary.

claude-code-skills.title: Anthropic, Extend Claude with skills (Claude Code documentation)

the-skill-scope-matrix-is-an-inference.header: The skill scope matrix is an inference
the-skill-scope-matrix-is-an-inference.description: no published framework combines the two axes into a 2x2 with care levels; the nearest are one-axis tier schemes [1]. Microsoft's zoned governance ties care to audience for agents, not skills: private personal agents, approved environments and admin approval for shared ones [2]. Label the square a rule of thumb.

skilldex.title: Saha and Hemanth, Skilldex: A Package Manager and Registry for Agent Skill Packages with Hierarchical Scope-Based Distribution

microsoft-zoned-governance.title: Microsoft, Implement a zoned governance strategy (Copilot Studio)

evals-matter-once-a-skill-is-shared.header: Evals matter once a skill is shared
evals-matter-once-a-skill-is-shared.description: 40 of 98 skills change sign between two harnesses running the same model, so a skill is best evaluated "with the model, agent, and repositories in which it will be deployed" [1].

swe-skills-bench.title: Han et al., SWE-Skills-Bench: Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?

two-questions.title: Two questions
two-questions.script: Here is a decision tool, and it asks two questions. Who uses the skill, only you or others too? And where, in any project or in one in particular?

four-squares.title: Four squares
four-squares.script: Four squares come out of that. Personal and project-specific: keep the details with the skill. Personal and general: keep reusable details nearby. Shared and project-specific: a project can share a skill and its supporting files. Shared and general: a team may choose a managed package and track its owner, version and evaluations. Moving a skill into shared use does not mean stripping project details; make its intended scope clear.

a-rule-of-thumb.title: A rule of thumb
a-rule-of-thumb.script: This matrix is a rule of thumb, and the label is mine. It is how I think about it, so try it on your own skills and tell me where it breaks.
